speaker: Doctor
text: How old are you, and do you have any history of trauma, gout, or autoimmune diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are you experiencing morning stiffness in your left knee, and does the joint appear visibly red or feel warm to the touch? REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP, Rheumatoid Factor, and Anti-CCP.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate: Slightly elevated; C-Reactive_Protein: Within normal limits; Rheumatoid Factor: Not in data; Anti-CCP: Not in data

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the inflammatory markers are only mildly elevated and negative for rheumatoid arthritis, does the knee pain improve with rest or worsen with activity, and do you notice any visible swelling or a limp? REQUEST TEST: HLA-B27, X-Ray_left_knee, and Urinalysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: HLA-B27: Not in data; X-Ray_Left_Knee: A lytic lesion in the distal femur near the knee joint with a thin rim of bone on the external surface and a 'soap bubble' appearance; Urinalysis: Not in data

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Tumor of Bone (GCT).

REQUEST IMAGES: Please confirm if the "soap bubble" appearance on the X-ray is visible and if there is any cortical breakthrough or soft tissue mass.
